title: Single-Phase Center-Tapped Transformer
summary: An Electric Machines design-and-fabrication project linking winding calculations and material selection with physical construction, tests and practical redesign.
overview: This Electric Machines project covered the design and fabrication of a single-phase center-tapped transformer with a 220 V primary supply and an E-I laminated core. The report connects voltage and load requirements with core and winding calculations, turns per volt, current ratings and wire-gauge selection. The supplied photograph shows the fabricated hardware.
approach: Started from the load and voltage requirements of the academic design brief.
Calculated core size, turns per volt, winding turns, current ratings and wire-gauge requirements.
Fabricated and insulated the windings, then assembled the laminated core and mounting hardware.
Included open-circuit and short-circuit tests in the project scope and redesigned the bobbin/core arrangement when the first winding fit proved impractical.
outcomes: Produced the fabricated transformer shown in the project photograph.
Connected analytical sizing decisions to practical winding, insulation and core-assembly constraints.
The report records a practical redesign after winding/core fit difficulties; exact measured test results are not established in the supplied report.

evidenceNotes: CVs and report calculations give 380 V secondary with a 220 V tap, while current owner wording is center-tapped. Exact secondary-output/topology specifications are excluded pending owner reconciliation. Initial calculation and redesigned calculation also use different apparent-power ratings.
Report page 14 has an open/short-circuit test heading but no visible recorded measurements. User-supplied project description supports test scope; no measured results are claimed.
General supporting power-grid diagram voltages are not fabricated-device ratings.
Photograph winding-label names and identifiers were sanitized in the public copy.
